lesson_evidence.heading: A direction a matrix preserves
lesson_evidence.exact_excerpt:
An eigenvector is a special exception: the result has the same direction, possibly reversed, and only its scale changes. The defining equation is

$$Av=\lambda v.$$

Here $v$ is the eigenvector and the scalar $\lambda$ is its associated eigenvalue. The requirement $v\ne0$ matters.

lesson_evidence.heading: Assumptions and asymptotic rate
lesson_evidence.exact_excerpt:
For a real symmetric matrix, power iteration generally reduces direction error asymptotically at a rate governed by

$$\left|\frac{\lambda_2}{\lambda_1}\right|^k.$$

This statement requires a unique dominant magnitude, a non-zero initial projection onto $v_1$, and no zero iterate $Ax_k$. It is an asymptotic description, not an unconditional finite-iteration error bound.
